newsitem.title: DUBAI: GM says consumer confidence in Gulf improves.
newsitem.headline: GM says consumer confidence in Gulf improves.

text.p: General Motors said there had been an improvement in consumer confidence in its Middle East Gulf market in the first half of this year.
"Our results -- and those of some other manufacturers -- during the first six months of 1997 illustrate a genuine improvement in market sentiment," regional director Alan Batey said in a statement.
"People now appear to be more willing to make important purchases, such as new cars."
Batey said this was particularly noticeable in recent weeks, a time of year when sales are traditionally slow.
GM sales in June were 37 percent higher than in June 1996, the statement said, but did not give total units sold.

Gulf Chevrolet Lumina sales in June were the highest of the year, up 27 percent on May. GM said the Chevrolet Cavalier in June enjoyed its highest monthly total since its 1995 introduction. Sales were 45 percent up on May.
GM said nearly 900 units of the Chevrolet Caprice were sold in June, compared to 740 in the same month last year.
"In general, I believe this kind of growth will continue and the pace may even pick up," Batey said.
In the trucks and sports utility sector, first half sales of the GMC Yukon four wheel drive rose 207 percent over first half 1996.
"Cadillac sales have been equally dramatic with the Deville and the DeVille Concours both showing six-month increases of nearly 50 percent over last year," GM said.
The six Gulf states are Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Oman. The Gulf is GM's biggest export market.
